bluf: Bloofusion is a German performance agency with offices in Emsdetten and Münster, ownership not disclosed, selling SEO and SEA as its two lead lines to small and large firms across DACH, with AI consulting, GEO, CRO, web analytics and social ads behind them. The record shows it moving into AI on both sides of the search result, a GEO/LLMO page and a ChatGPT Ads service, and marketing itself through its BLOO:CON event, the Search Camp podcast and 15 LinkedIn ads. A rival should know its client book on record is empty and three of five tested lines, AI search, paid social and CRO, are contradicted by its own house.
doing:
The positioning line, a performance focused online marketing agency optimising SEO, SEA, social, web analytics and CRO for small and large firms across DACH, decodes as a search first performance shop that sells to any size of client in the German speaking market. The headline claim, quoted as a claim: the leading agency for online performance, backed by more than 20 years in online marketing.

Two lines score 3: Paid Search (the homepage title names SEA, with a Google Ads management page plus account audit and feed optimisation subpages) and SEO (an SEO page plus audit, international, local, linkbuilding and relaunch subpages). Five core lines score 2: AI Automation / Agents (a KI consulting page selling AI audience building, image generation and process automation), AI Search / GEO (a GEO/LLMO page targeting AI Overviews, ChatGPT, Gemini and Perplexity, plus a separate ChatGPT Ads page), CRO (landing page optimisation, CRO audits and accessibility audits), Data & Measurement (GA4 setup and audits, GTM consulting, server side tagging, dashboards, 24/7 monitoring) and Paid Social (Meta, LinkedIn, TikTok and Pinterest, with Conversion API and account audit subpages). The one proprietary product is 24/7-Sentinel, always on tracking monitoring on the web analytics page. No partners are listed.

AI posture in plain terms: it sells AI three ways, as consulting (audiences, image generation, automation), as GEO/LLMO for AI search, and as early ChatGPT Ads management; the Horus move read marks P8 making and P1 partial, since no audited AI visibility product shows. Pricing signals: the about section links a pricing page promising transparent, fair prices, but figures were not captured and the move read records no public pricing model. Recent moves: none dated; news, case studies and jobs are empty. Conspicuously absent for a performance agency: a single named client on record, any feed, schema or entity service despite the feed optimisation subpage, and Programmatic & CTV, Retail Media and Web & Product all at 0.
clients:
The record describes a mixed client type, small and large firms in its own words, with verticals of ecommerce and B2B, a home market of Germany with offices in Emsdetten and Münster, and a DACH wide claim in the positioning line. The book on record is empty: 0 clients, 0 observed, 0 named only, no mix, no top needs and no shared clients, even though a references page (ueber-uns/referenzen) sits among the sources the record lists. No case study title, URL slug or press line names anyone, so no need code is assigned to any client, observed or inferred, and no client on this book can appear on another tracked agency's book.

Inferred from the sold mix, and said as such: a client that buys from this agency most plausibly comes for paid performance (N2) or organic demand (N1), the two lines that score 3, with AI and automation (N9) the line it is adding on top. Nothing in the record confirms that for any named company, and the share of the book that is names only cannot be stated for a book of 0.

What the base needs next, as a judgment tied to the edition: the Horus read places the agency best for KJ1 (the click is being replaced by the citation) and KJ2 (ads inside AI answers scale faster than any channel before them), both driven by its AI Search and Paid Search lines, and most exposed to KJ6 (the agency middle is being hollowed out) through those same paid search and SEO hours. Its DACH ecommerce and B2B clients are therefore likely to ask for citation visibility and assistant ad tests next, which its GEO and ChatGPT Ads pages already sell; moderate confidence, because no client engagement is described anywhere in the record.
house: Say and do: 2 of 5 tested lines practised on its own house. AI Search / GEO is contradicted: it sells AI visibility and publishes no llms.txt, with 3 AI topic URLs in its sitemap and no AI crawlers blocked. Paid Social is contradicted: no social ad pixel on its own site. CRO is contradicted: no testing tool detected on its own homepage. LinkedIn advertising is corroborated: the library shows 15 ads, 11 company page ads and 4 thought leader ads by staff, one reading "Du bist Online-Marketer:in und willst 2026 richtig durchstarten?", promoting events and YouTube tips. Paid Search is unknown: the Transparency Center lookup was blocked. Publishing cadence is corroborated: the sitemap lists 253 URLs, 6 updated in 90 days and 121 in 365 days. Tags are gtm and usercentrics, no CMS recorded, no test tools, ABM stack or social pixels; Meta and TikTok status not recorded; social links LinkedIn, Instagram, YouTube and Facebook.

openings:
The strongest opening is the contradiction set: Bloofusion sells CRO with no testing tool on its own homepage, AI visibility with no llms.txt, and paid social with no social pixel on its own site. A rival whose own house passes those tests can very likely lead with them against a self described leading agency for online performance (moderate confidence). Falsifier: a testing tool, llms.txt and social pixel on bloofusion.de at the next compile.

It sells AI search with no audited AI visibility product on record, so a rival with citation share, a scorecard or tracking leads with the number (likely); no feed, schema or entity work shows despite a feed optimisation subpage (low confidence). Pricing is a public gap: the about section promises transparent, fair prices, no figures were captured and the move read finds no public model, so a rival publishing prices takes the word from it. Monsoon reads Onshore wind at 58.8 with 55% of movable work pointing to Eastern Europe, so an offshore delivered SEA and SEO offer likely undercuts the Paid Search hours its KJ6 exposure rests on. With no client named anywhere, every account it holds is contestable by a rival who can find one.
